title: Motion for Temporary Orders Regarding Custody and Support
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF TARRANT COUNTY, TEXAS
360TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. 2024-12345-360

IN THE INTEREST OF LILY R. CARTER AND JACK T. CARTER, CHILDREN

MOTION FOR TEMPORARY ORDERS

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

NOW COMES Alistair Finch, hereinafter referred to as Movant, and files this Motion for Temporary Orders in the above-styled and numbered cause, and in support thereof would show the Court as follows:

I.
Movant is an individual whose date of birth is August 4, 1982. Movant resides at 742 Evergreen Terrace, Fort Worth, Texas 76102. Movant is the father of the minor children, Lily R. Carter and Jack T. Carter.

II.
The Respondent, Margaret H. Carter, is the mother of the minor children and resides at 1889 Magnolia Lane, Arlington, Texas 76013. Respondent's Social Security Number is 467-82-1935.

III.
The parties were divorced by Decree of Divorce entered on January 15, 2023, in this Court. Since the divorce, Respondent has repeatedly denied Movant possession of the children without just cause. Movant seeks immediate temporary orders to establish a possession schedule.

IV.
Movant requests that the Court enter temporary orders granting Movant possession of the children every first, third, and fifth weekend of each month, as well as alternating holidays and extended summer possession. The parties attended mediation on March 1, 2024, with Bates Mediation Services, LLC, but failed to reach an agreement.

V.
Movant is employed by Lone Star Energy Solutions, Inc., a company d/b/a Texas Power Direct, as a Senior Engineer. Movant has historically paid child support in the amount of $1,200 per month. However, Respondent has failed to provide an accounting of how those funds are spent.

VI.
As temporary relief, Movant requests that Respondent be ordered to provide a full accounting of all child support payments received. See In re Carter, 589 S.W.3d 214 (Tex. App.—Fort Worth 2019). Courts have consistently held that a parent has the right to know how support is used for the benefit of the child. See also Finch v. Finch, 456 S.W.3d 123 (Tex. App.—Dallas 2015).

VII.
Movant prays that citation and notice issue as required by law, and that upon hearing, the Court grant the following temporary orders: (a) appointing Movant and Respondent as Joint Managing Conservators, with Movant having the right to designate the children's primary residence; (b) establishing a possession schedule; (c) ordering Respondent to pay child support; (d) ordering Respondent to maintain health insurance for the children; and (e) such other relief to which Movant may show himself entitled.

Respectfully submitted,

[Signature]

Alistair Finch
Pro Se
742 Evergreen Terrace
Fort Worth, Texas 76102
(817) 555-0198
Email: alistair.finch@email.com

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I certify that a true copy of this Motion was sent to counsel for Respondent, Rhonda P. Vance, at 100 Justice Parkway, Suite 400, Fort Worth, Texas 76102, on April 4, 2024 via e-filing.

[Signature]

Alistair Finch

title: Response to Motion for Temporary Orders and Counter-Motion for Temporary Orders
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF DALLAS COUNTY, TEXAS
162ND JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. DC-24-07892

IN THE MATTER OF THE MARRIAGE OF
GRACE O. KLINE AND PETER J. KLINE
AND IN THE INTEREST OF ALEXA J. KLINE, CHILD

RESPONSE TO MOTION FOR TEMPORARY ORDERS AND COUNTER-MOTION

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

NOW COMES Grace O. Kline, Respondent and Counter-Movant herein, and files this Response to Peter J. Kline's Motion for Temporary Orders and Counter-Motion for Temporary Orders, and respectfully shows the Court:

I.
Respondent is an individual with a date of birth of November 30, 1985. Respondent resides at 5500 Preston Road, Apt. 2101, Dallas, Texas 75205. Respondent is the mother of the child, Alexa J. Kline.

II.
Petitioner, Peter J. Kline, is the father of the child and resides at 2211 Commerce Street, Dallas, Texas 75201. Petitioner's Social Security Number is 458-71-2233. Petitioner is employed by Kline Holdings, LLC, a real estate investment firm.

III.
The parties were married on June 12, 2010, and separated on February 1, 2024. Petitioner filed a Motion for Temporary Orders on March 10, 2024, seeking primary custody of the child. Respondent denies the allegations of instability made by Petitioner.

IV.
Respondent is employed as a registered nurse at Dallas Methodist Hospital, a facility operated by the HealthCorp Group, Inc., d/b/a Methodist Health System. Respondent has a stable work schedule and can provide a suitable home for the child.

V.
Respondent counter-moves for temporary orders granting her sole managing conservatorship of the child, with Petitioner receiving supervised visitation due to his history of substance abuse. Respondent requests that Petitioner submit to random drug testing as a condition of visitation. See Kline v. Kline, 712 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. App.—Dallas 2022). The court in Grayson v. Grayson, 398 S.W.3d 789 (Tex. App.—Houston [14th Dist.] 2013), held that drug testing may be ordered when credible evidence of abuse is presented.

VI.
Respondent also requests temporary spousal support pursuant to Tex. Fam. Code § 8.051, as Petitioner has historically been the primary breadwinner and Respondent has reduced her hours to care for the child.

VII.
Respondent prays that the Court deny Petitioner's Motion for Temporary Orders, and grant the Counter-Motion for Temporary Orders as set forth above.

Respectfully submitted,

[Signature]

Grace O. Kline
Pro Se
5500 Preston Road, Apt. 2101
Dallas, Texas 75205
Phone: (214) 555-2378
Email: grace.kline@email.org

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I certify that a true copy of this document was served on Petitioner's counsel, Dean A. Mitchell, at 300 Main Street, Suite 1200, Dallas, Texas 75202, on March 20, 2024.

[Signature]

Grace O. Kline

title: Motion for Temporary Orders Regarding Domestic Violence Protection
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF TRAVIS COUNTY, TEXAS
427TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. D-1-FM-24-005432

IN THE MATTER OF THE MARRIAGE OF
ELENA M. REYES AND JOSÉ L. REYES

MOTION FOR TEMPORARY ORDERS (PROTECTIVE RELIEF)

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

NOW COMES Elena M. Reyes, Movant, and files this Motion for Temporary Orders seeking protective relief from José L. Reyes, Respondent, and in support thereof shows:

I.
Movant is a person with a date of birth of March 15, 1990, residing at 1225 Congress Avenue, Austin, Texas 78701. Movant is the spouse of Respondent.

II.
Respondent is José L. Reyes, residing at 5678 Riverside Drive, Austin, Texas 78704. Respondent's Social Security Number is 556-43-2890.

III.
The parties were married on October 10, 2018, and separated on April 1, 2024, following an incident of family violence. On March 28, 2024, Respondent physically assaulted Movant, resulting in injuries documented by Austin Police Department Case Report #2024-3892.

IV.
Movant seeks a temporary protective order prohibiting Respondent from committing further acts of violence, communicating with Movant except through counsel, and requiring Respondent to vacate the former marital residence. Movant also requests temporary spousal support and exclusive use of the residence.

V.
Movant is employed by Texas State University as an adjunct professor. Respondent is employed by Reyes Construction Corp., d/b/a Reyes Building Solutions, as a project manager.

VI.
Movant cites the case of Reyes v. Reyes, 834 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. App.—Austin 2020), which established that a history of domestic violence is grounds for temporary protective orders. Additionally, the Court may consider analogous precedent from Sanchez v. Sanchez, 678 S.W.3d 234 (Tex. App.—San Antonio 2018). The relevant statutory authority is Tex. Fam. Code § 85.021, which outlines the requirements for a temporary ex parte protective order.

VII.
Movant prays that the Court issue temporary orders granting her exclusive possession of the residence located at 1225 Congress Avenue, spousal support of $3,000 per month, and a protective order lasting 60 days pending final hearing.

Respectfully submitted,

[Signature]

Elena M. Reyes
1225 Congress Avenue
Austin, Texas 78701
Phone: (512) 555-9142
Email: elena.reyes@utexas.edu

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I certify that a copy of this Motion was served upon Respondent's attorney, Martin D. Lake, at 200 West 6th Street, Suite 900, Austin, Texas 78701, on April 2, 2024.

[Signature]

Elena M. Reyes

title: Motion for Temporary Orders regarding Child Support and Medical Insurance
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF HARRIS COUNTY, TEXAS
311TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. 2024-56789-311

IN THE INTEREST OF AIDEN J. GRIFFIN AND
MAYA S. GRIFFIN, CHILDREN

MOTION FOR TEMPORARY ORDERS

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

NOW COMES Daniel T. Griffin, Movant, and files this Motion for Temporary Orders against Respondent, Natalie R. Griffin, and would respectfully show the Court:

I.
Movant is an individual born on July 22, 1981. Movant resides at 4500 Westheimer Road, Houston, Texas 77027. Movant is the father of the minor children, Aiden J. Griffin and Maya S. Griffin.

II.
Respondent is the mother of the children and resides at 1234 Bellaire Blvd., Houston, Texas 77401. Respondent's Social Security Number is 611-45-7890.

III.
The parties were never married but entered into a Suit Affecting Parent-Child Relationship on March 1, 2020. Since the filing of that suit, Respondent has failed to maintain stable employment and has not contributed to the children's expenses.

IV.
Movant requests that the Court enter temporary orders establishing Respondent's child support obligation based on her earning capacity. Movant has primary custody of the children and incurs all costs for housing, food, education, and medical care. Respondent's last known employer was Griffin Medical Equipment, d/b/a Griffin Home Health, but she was terminated in December 2023.

V.
Movant also requests that Respondent be ordered to provide medical insurance coverage for the children if available through any future employer. Movant cites the case of Griffin v. Griffin, 912 S.W.3d 678 (Tex. App.—Houston [14th Dist.] 2021), which holds that a parent may be imputed income if voluntarily unemployed. See also Dawson v. Dawson, 534 S.W.3d 512 (Tex. App.—Houston [1st Dist.] 2017). The applicable statute is Tex. Fam. Code § 154.063, regarding the ability to contribute to support.

VI.
Movant further requests that Respondent be ordered to pay 50% of the children's uninsured medical expenses and extracurricular activity fees, and that the Court order wage withholding through the Texas Child Support Disbursement Unit.

VII.
Movant prays that the Court set this matter for hearing and issue temporary orders consistent with the above requests.

Respectfully submitted,

[Signature]

Daniel T. Griffin
4500 Westheimer Road
Houston, Texas 77027
Phone: (713) 555-6723
Email: daniel.griffin@email.net

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I hereby certify that a copy of this Motion was served upon Respondent's attorney, Lisa M. Carter, at 1001 Fannin Street, Suite 500, Houston, Texas 77002, on May 10, 2024, via e-service.

[Signature]

Daniel T. Griffin

title: Motion for Temporary Orders for Exclusive Use of Marital Residence and Interim Attorney's Fees
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF BEXAR COUNTY, TEXAS
225TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. 2024-CI-09876

IN THE MATTER OF THE MARRIAGE OF
SOPHIA L. HARRISON AND MICHAEL K. HARRISON

MOTION FOR TEMPORARY ORDERS

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

NOW COMES Sophia L. Harrison, Petitioner, and files this Motion for Temporary Orders against Respondent, Michael K. Harrison, and in support thereof states:

I.
Petitioner is an individual with a date of birth of December 1, 1987. Petitioner resides at 9898 Broadway Street, San Antonio, Texas 78209. Petitioner and Respondent were married on May 25, 2014, and separated on June 1, 2024.

II.
Respondent is Michael K. Harrison, residing at the same address until he vacated on June 1, 2024. Respondent's current address is unknown. Respondent's Social Security Number is 679-23-4512.

III.
Petitioner seeks temporary orders granting her exclusive use and possession of the marital residence located at 9898 Broadway Street, San Antonio, Texas 78209, pending final division of property. Petitioner also seeks interim attorney's fees to be paid by Respondent.

IV.
Petitioner is a homemaker with no current income, while Respondent is employed by Harrison Financial Advisors, Inc., a company d/b/a Harrison Wealth Management. Respondent has substantial income and assets, including a 401(k) account valued at $250,000.

V.
Petitioner requests interim spousal support in the amount of $4,000 per month to maintain the status quo during the divorce proceedings. Pursuant to Tex. Fam. Code § 6.502, the Court may award temporary spousal maintenance based on the needs of the requesting party and the ability of the other party to pay.

VI.
Petitioner cites the cases of Harrison v. Harrison, 845 S.W.3d 567 (Tex. App.—San Antonio 2021), which affirms the court's authority to grant exclusive use of the marital residence, and Benson v. Benson, 678 S.W.3d 345 (Tex. App.—El Paso 2019), regarding interim attorney's fees.

VII.
Petitioner prays that the Court issue temporary orders granting her exclusive use of the residence, spousal support of $4,000 per month, and interim attorney's fees in the amount of $10,000.

Respectfully submitted,

[Signature]

Sophia L. Harrison
9898 Broadway Street
San Antonio, Texas 78209
Phone: (210) 555-4102
Email: sophia.harrison@email.co

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I certify that a true copy of this Motion was served on Respondent's counsel, David A. Turner, at 500 Commerce Street, Suite 200, San Antonio, Texas 78205, on June 5, 2024, via certified mail.

[Signature]

Sophia L. Harrison
